gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much power each 10Gbps switch can give to four devices: UGREEN's manual rates the CM691's power input at 5 V 2.4 A max for the whole switch, ATEN says the US3342 needs at least 5 V 3 A for basic USB functions, and Cable Matters adds an optional power port that it recommends for power-hungry devices such as external hard drives.
standout_why: Compared against the two cited UGREEN product pages and the top results. The UGREEN product pages (us.ugreen.com, both URLs) returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I could not check their text. Digital Desk Solutions (2026-10-28) says 'Power source not listed' for the 10Gbps CM691 listing and lists 'Per-port speed split not spelled out' as a con for the 7-port model. It also says 'Nobody on the team used or measured these units', and its only current figure is a generic 900 mA example. PicksLab (2026-03-12) covers no 10Gbps model and gives no current or wattage for any switch. TechWise covers only video KVMs and says nothing about bus power, bandwidth sharing or SSDs. ChatGPT's own answers disagree with each other: one says the UGREEN 'relies on host USB power', another calls external power 'important for SSD stability', and none gives a number. None of these pages states a power budget for the 10Gbps switches.
decides: This confirms the CM691 as the pick for a keyboard, mouse and one portable SSD, with one condition the page has to state: the whole switch runs on 5 V 2.4 A max (12 W) through its USB-C input, and that power is shared by all four device ports. For a desk that will also run a webcam, a bus-powered hard drive or a second drive, it points to a switch with an optional or included power input: Cable Matters 201160 (adapter not included) or UGREEN's 2-in-7-out 10Gbps model (adapter included). ATEN US3342 is fair as the premium option only if the shopper uses its USB-C power input. Its basic USB functions need at least 5 V 3 A, and its pass-through charges a laptop at up to 85 W from a 65 W+ adapter.

findings.label: Power input for the whole switch
findings.note: Manual spec line: 'Power Supply Input USB-C 5.0V 2.4A Max'. 5 V × 2.4 A = 12 W, shared by all four device ports (1× USB-C, 3× USB-A). The manual gives no per-port current.

findings.label: Data rate as rated
findings.value: Up to 10 Gbps (USB 3.2 Gen 2); per-port vs shared not stated
findings.note: The manual footnote says 'The data are measured by UGREEN lab but may vary based on specific circumstances.'

findings.label: Minimum power for basic USB functions
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through · ATEN
findings.note: The ATEN page also says 'No drivers or external power adapter needed'. Its power consumption is listed as 'DC5V:0.43W', which ATEN describes as typical with no external load.

findings.label: Laptop charging pass-through
findings.value: USB-C PD 3.0 up to 85 W, needs a separate single-port USB-C PD adapter over 65 W
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through · ATEN
findings.note: Power input is one USB-C port with PD 3.0 at 5/9/15/20 V. The adapter is not in the box: the package lists 2× 1 m USB-C 3.2 Gen 2 cables, a remote port selector and instructions.

findings.label: Device ports
findings.value: 3× USB-A + 1× USB-C, all USB 3.2 Gen 2 (up to 10 Gbps); host ports 2× USB-C, data only
findings.source_title: US3342 2-Port USB-C Gen 2 Sharing Switch with Power Pass-through · ATEN
findings.note: Corrects our current page, which says '4 (listings say USB-A)'. ATEN says the host USB-C ports do not support a USB-C monitor.

findings.label: Power input
findings.value: Optional power port, adapter not included; Cable Matters recommends it for power-hungry devices such as external hard drives and to avoid connection problems when host power is insufficient
findings.source_title: 4 Port USB-A & USB-C Switch with Remote Control · Cable Matters
findings.note: The maker page gives no voltage or current for the port. The page shows no price; the Cable Matters store button reads 'Out of stock' and the Amazon button reads 'In stock'.

findings.source_title: 4 Port USB-A & USB-C Switch with Remote Control · Cable Matters

findings.source_title: 4 Port USB-A & USB-C Switch with Remote Control · Cable Matters
